reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted interval work focused on threshold and high-end aerobic power, crucial for improving speed on technical trails. Plan B, while including a longer run and tempo session, relies heavily on longer, moderate-intensity sessions which are less effective for developing the specific physiological adaptations needed for faster trail running. Plan A’s structured approach with dedicated interval days and strength work directly addresses the athlete’s goal of increasing speed, while Plan B’s emphasis on volume could lead to overtraining and reduced effectiveness. Furthermore, Plan A’s inclusion of cross-training helps to manage fatigue and prevent overuse injuries, a key consideration for trail runners.
